J.- Through this revision petition, the petitioners have assailed the legality and validity of the judgment and decrce dated 23.11.2020, passed by the learned Additional District Judge-II, Karak, whereby the petitioners' appeal was dismissed, and thc judgment and decree of the learned Senior Civil Judge, Karak, dated 18.02.2000, was upheld. Through the said judgment, the suit filed by plaintiffs/respondents No.l to 3 was decreed against the p etiti oners/cle fendants.

2. Ihe brief'facts leading to the f,rling of the present revision petition are that the plaintiffs/respondents No.l to 3, namely Muhamrnad Gul and two others (hereinafter ^ Page-2-ofl0 referred to as "the respondents"), instituted a suit against the defendants, Lal Zaman and others (hereinafter referred to as "the petitioners"), seeking a declaration along with perpetual, prohibitory, and mandatory injunctions in respect of the suit property. The respondents asserted that their predecessor-in-interest, Sher Azam alias Telephone, as reflected in the Jamabandi for the year 1965-66, was the owner in possession of property measuring 6-Kanal and 8-Marla (1l3rd share) out of a total area of 19-Kanal and 3-Marla, comprising V Klrata Nos. 741 and 742, Khasra Nos. 2329,2330, and 2341, situated in Mauza Land Kamar, District Karak. It was further contended that, in the subsequent settlement, the earlier Khata and Khasra numbers were renumbered in the Jamabandi for the year 1974-75, as Khata No.328, comprising Khasra No. 5727 measuring 8-Kanal and 15- Marla, and Khata No.329, comprising Khasra Nos. 5725, 5726,5773, and 5786 measuring l0-Kanal and l5-Marla, situated in Mauza Warana Ahmad Abad, District Karak. It is pertinent to mention here that, in the Jamabandi for the year 20ll-12, the earlier Khata Nos. 328 and 329 were renumbered as Khata Nos. 364 and 365, respectively. The respondents further contended that they had transferred one-third share each in Khata Nos. 328 and329 to Lal Zaman (del'endant No.l/respondent No.4). A.

Page-3-of10 However, I.al Zaman, without any lawful authority, illegally transferred one-half share in Khata No. 329, comprising Khasra Nos. 5725, 5726, 5773, and 5786, in favour of the petitioners (Abdul Jabbar and others) through Mutation No. 507 dated 30.07.1978 (Ex.PW2/3). Consequently, the said mutation and the resultant revenue entries are elroneous and liable to be set aside and corrected in accordance with law.

3. The petitioners were summoned; they appeared and contested the suit by submitting the written O statement. The divergent pleadings of the parties culminated in the framing of various issues. After recording evidence and hearing the arguments of learned counsel for the parlies, the suit of the respondents was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 18.02.2020. Then petitioners challenged this decision through Appeal No. 39113 of 2020, which was subsequently dismissed by the Additional District Judge-II, Karak, vide judgment and decree dated 23.11.2020. This led to the filing of the present revision petition.
4. Arguments heard and carefully perused the case record with the valuable assistance of learned counsel for the parties.

5. It is evident from the record that the respondents' IJ .t tl Page-4-ofl0 predecessor-in-interest, Sher Azam alias Telephone, had purchased, through Mutation No. 33486 attested on 14.09.1962 (Ex. PWZI6), property measuring 6-Kanal and 8-Marla, representing one-third share out of the total area measuring l9-Kanal and 3-Marlas, comprising Khata Nos. 741 and 742, Khasra Nos. 2329, 2330, and 2341, situated inMauzaland Kamar, District Karak. The record reflects that Sher Azam, also known as "Telephone," sold the said one-third share to Lal Zaman (defendant No.l / respondent No.4), through a sale Mutation No. 36429, attested on 13.12.1968. In this mutation, the original Khata numbers 741 and 742listed in column 2 were changed to new Khata numbers 328 and 329 in column 8. In other words, the respondents' predecessor, Sher Azam, had purchased a property measuring 6-Kanals and 8-Marla in the disputed Khata and Khasra numbers in 1962.I{owever, he sold the said property in 1968 and thereafter ceased to own even an inch of it.

6. The available record further demonstrates that the Khata and Khasra numbers, along with the corresponding area) recorded in the Jamabandi for the year 1965-66, were subsequently altered in the Jamabandi for the years, 1974-75, and 20ll-12. Page-6-of10 year 1965-66 (Ex.PW-217), the disputed property was recorded under two Khata numbers, 741 and 742, and comprised three Khasra numbers i.e. 2329, 2330, and 2341, covering a total area of l9-Kanal and 3-Marla. However, in the subsequent Jamabandi for the year 7974- 75, (Ex.PW-2/8), both Khata numbers were renumbered as 328 and 329. During this revision, Khata No. 741, which previously included Khasra No. 2329 measuring 9-Kanals, was renumbered as new Khata No. 328, and the said Khasra was correspondingly assigned a new I number, Khasra No. 5727, measuring 8-Kanal and 15- Marla. As a result of this change, a decrease of 5-Marla in area occurred. l,ikewise, Khasra No. 2330, which earlier measured 2-Kanal and 15-Mar1a, was subdivided into three new Khasra numbers, 5725, measuring 9- Marlas and classified as Banjar Qadeem, 5773, measuring l8-Marla and classified as Ghair Mumkin Rasta (thoroughfare), and 5726, measuring 2-Kanal and classified as Barani (rain-fed agricultural land). The total area of these newly created Khasra numbers amounted to 3-Kanal and 7-Marla, showing an increase of l2-Marla from the earlier record, however, there is no evidence to suggest that the aforesaid increase or decrease pertains to the property of the respondents' predecessor, Sher Azam alias Telephone, who, during his lifetime, had sold his ^ Pagc-7-of10 property measuring 6-Kanal, 8-Marla, to the defendant/respondent No. 4, Lal Zaman.

8. The respondents asserted that their predecessor-ininterest, Sher Azam, had alienated one-third share each in Khata Nos. 328 and 329 in favour of Lal Zaman (defendant No.l/respondent No.4). It was fuither alleged that I"al Zaman, acting without lawful authority, subsequently transferred one-half share in Khata No. 329, comprising Khasra Nos. 5725,5726,5773, and 5786, to the petitioners, namely Abdul Jabbar and others, through Mutation No. 507 dated 30.07.1978. I{owever, this contention is devoid of merit. The record clearly shows that the fluctuations in the area and entries pertaining to the disputed Khata and Khasra numbers occurred during a period when Sher Azam alias "Telephone" neither held ownership nor was in possession of any portion of the disputed property. Moreover, mutation No. 507 dated 30.07.1978 (Iix.PW2l3), perLains to a sale transaction between Lal Zaman (incorrectly recorded as Lal Zameer) and the petitioners. If any effor or incorrect entry exists in this mutation, such a mistake cannot be interpreted or extended to the benefit of the respondents-or any third party 9. Legally speaking, effoneous entries in the revenue record arising out of settlement proceedings can be n Pagc-8-of10 rectified only if the entire affected property, along with both the existing and previous landowners, is included in a suit instituted within the prescribed period of limitation, which is not the case in the present matter.

10. The pivotal issue of limitation has been erroneously decided by both the Courts below in a slipshod and cursory manner. It is settled law that in cases involving mere correction of entries in the revenue record, each ncw adverse entry in the record of rights (Jamabandi) gives rise to a fresh cause of action only for a person who is in possession of the land to which such entry relates. I{owever, the record clearly reveals that the respondents' predecessor-in-interest was neither the owner nor in possession of the suit property. Despite this, the respondents havc sought to challenge the disputed entries in the rcvenue record pertaining to the ycars 1974 and 1978, through the present suit instituted on 13.1 I .2014, which is hopelessly time-barred and, therefore, the concurrent findings of both courts below, holding that a recurring cause of action existed, are erroneous, misconccived, and not sustainable in law. The impugned judgments are liable to be set aside on this ground alone. Iteliance is placed on the judgments reported as '6Principal Public School, Sangota, a Government of Khybcr Pakhtunkhwa through Chief n Page-9-ofl0 Secretary and others Vs Sarbiland and others", (2022 SCMR 189) and 'I(han Muhammad and others Vs Mst. Khatoon Bibi and others", (2017 SCMR 1476)

11. Admittedly, the alleged incorrcct entries in the revenue record were never questioned or challenged by the respondents' predecessor-in-interest, Sher Azam alias Telephone, during his lifetime. Ncither the plaint nor the evidence adduced reflects any plausible reason for such omission. In the absence of any explanation as to why T Sher Azam failed to contest the alleged erroneous entries during his lifetime, the respondents, being his successorsin-interest, had no lctcus standi to assail the same through the present proceedings. The settled law is that where a predecessor has acquiesced in or failed to challenge the revenue entries during his lifetime, his successors cannot subsequently reopen the matter without demonstrating fraud, misreprcsentation, or other sufficient cause. Reliance is placed on the judgments reported as "Mst. Faheeman Begum and others Vs Islam-ud-Din and others", (2023 SCMR 1402), "Gulam Abbas and others Vs Muhammad Shafi & others", (2016 SCMR 1403), o'Noor Din and another Vs Additional District Judge, Lahore", (2014 SCMR 513), and "Muhammad Rustam and another Vs Mst. Makhan Jan and others", (2013 SCMR 299).

f /\ Page - 10 - of 10 12. For the foregoing reasons, the revision petition is allowed. The concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the Appellate Court are hereby set aside. Consequently, the suit filed by the respondents stands dismissed. There shall be no order as to costs.
